[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.95]\coordinate (A) at (0,2.344);\coordinate (C) at (0,0);\coordinate (Bp) at (3,0);\coordinate (Hz) at (3.85,2.344);\draw[dashed] (A)--(Hz);\draw (A)--(C);\draw (C)--(Bp);\draw (A)--(Bp);\coordinate (rqa) at ($(C)!0.25cm!(A)$);\coordinate (rqb) at ($(C)!0.25cm!(Bp)$);\draw (rqa)--($(rqa)+(rqb)-(C)$)--(rqb);\pic[draw,"$\theta$",angle radius=0.8cm,angle eccentricity=1.45] {angle=Bp--A--Hz};\node[above left] at (A) {Climber};\node[below right] at (Bp) {Swimmer};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A climber at the top of a cliff is looking at a swimmer below. What is the marked angle $\theta$?

options.why: Names the angle from the observer being high up; an angle of elevation opens upwards, and here the line of sight goes down from the horizontal.

options.text: Neither an angle of elevation nor an angle of depression
options.why: Reads the dashed line as the vertical cliff face; the arc here starts at the horizontal, which is what these angles are measured from.

questions.solution_text:
$\theta$ is at the climber's eye, between the dashed horizontal and the line of sight.
The swimmer is below the climber, so the climber turns downwards.
$\theta$ is an angle of depression.

options.why: Measures from the vertical cliff face $AC$ instead of from the horizontal $AH$.
Puts the angle at the swimmer; that is the angle of elevation of $A$ from $B$.
Names the right angle at the base of the cliff, which is not a line-of-sight angle at all.

questions.solution_text:
The angle of depression is at $A$, between the horizontal $AH$ and the line of sight $AB$.
The angle of depression of $B$ from $A$ is $\angle HAB$.

options.text: It is measured from the vertical tower wall, not from the horizontal at $A$.
It is measured at $A$ instead of at $B$.
options.why: Places the angle of depression at the object; an angle of depression is always at the observer, which is $A$ here.

options.text: It is measured to the horizontal at $B$, not to the line of sight.
options.why: Misreads which two lines bound $\theta$; both of its arms meet at $A$, and one of them is the line of sight.

options.text: It is too large to be an angle of depression.
options.why: Judges the angle by its size; what disqualifies $\theta$ is the line it is measured from, not how big it is.

questions.solution_text:
$\theta$ lies between the tower wall $AC$ and the line of sight $AB$.
The tower wall is vertical, and angles of elevation and depression are measured from the horizontal.
The angle of depression is $90^{\circ}-\theta$.

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.95]\coordinate (A) at (0,1.875);\coordinate (C) at (0,0);\coordinate (Bp) at (3,0);\coordinate (Hz) at (3.85,1.875);\draw[dashed] (A)--(Hz);\draw (A)--(C);\draw (C)--(Bp);\draw (A)--(Bp);\coordinate (rqa) at ($(C)!0.25cm!(A)$);\coordinate (rqb) at ($(C)!0.25cm!(Bp)$);\draw (rqa)--($(rqa)+(rqb)-(C)$)--(rqb);\pic[draw,"$58^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.72cm,angle eccentricity=1.6] {angle=C--A--Bp};\node[above left] at (A) {Climber};\node[below right] at (Bp) {Swimmer};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
At the top of a cliff the angle between the cliff face and the line of sight to a swimmer is $58^{\circ}$. Find the angle of depression of the swimmer from the cliff top.

options.why: Reads the marked angle as the answer; it is measured from the vertical cliff face, not from the horizontal.
Subtracts from $180^{\circ}$ instead of from the $90^{\circ}$ between the vertical cliff face and the horizontal.

questions.solution_text:
The cliff face and the horizontal meet at $90^{\circ}$.
$\theta+58^{\circ}=90^{\circ}$
$\theta=90^{\circ}-58^{\circ}$
$=32^{\circ}$

\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.95]\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\coordinate (F) at (3.2,0);\coordinate (T) at (3.2,1.425);\draw (-0.35,0)--(O);\draw (O)--(F);\draw[dashed] (F)--(4,0);\draw (F)--(T);\draw (O)--(T);\coordinate (rqa) at ($(F)!0.25cm!(O)$);\coordinate (rqb) at ($(F)!0.25cm!(T)$);\draw (rqa)--($(rqa)+(rqb)-(F)$)--(rqb);\pic[draw,"$66^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.7cm,angle eccentricity=1.5] {angle=O--T--F};\node[below left] at (O) {$O$};\node[below right] at (F) {$F$};\node[above right] at (T) {$T$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A hot-air balloon at $T$ is directly above $F$, and an observer stands at $O$. At the balloon the angle between the vertical $TF$ and the line of sight $TO$ is $66^{\circ}$. Find the angle of elevation of the balloon from $O$.

options.why: Copies the marked angle; that angle is at the balloon and is measured from the vertical $TF$.
Subtracts $66^{\circ}$ from $180^{\circ}$ without also subtracting the right angle at $F$.
Treats the two angles as complementary; they are alternate angles on parallel horizontals, so they are equal.
Treats the two angles as supplementary and subtracts from $180^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
The horizontal at $A$ is parallel to the sea at $B$, and $AB$ is a transversal.
The angle of elevation $=29^{\circ}$, alternate angles on parallel lines

A hiker looks up at a hot-air balloon at an angle of elevation of $37^{\circ}$. Which diagram shows this?

options.why: Measures the $37^{\circ}$ from the dashed vertical instead of from the horizontal ground.
Marks the angle at the balloon rather than at the hiker, which gives an angle of depression.

questions.solution_text:
In $A$ the angle is measured from a vertical, so it is neither an elevation nor a depression.
In $C$ the angle is at the top, measured down from the horizontal, so it is an angle of depression.
In $B$ the angle is at the hiker, measured up from the horizontal ground to the line of sight, so $B$ is correct.

options.why: Uses the marked angle directly; it is measured from the vertical tower wall rather than from a horizontal.
Subtracts $71^{\circ}$ from $180^{\circ}$ instead of from the $90^{\circ}$ at the top of the tower.

questions.solution_text:
$d=90^{\circ}-71^{\circ}$
$=19^{\circ}$
The horizontal at $A$ is parallel to the ground at $B$.
The angle of elevation $=19^{\circ}$, alternate angles on parallel lines

options.why: Takes the complement, as if the angle of elevation and the angle of depression added to $90^{\circ}$.
Takes the supplement, subtracting the angle of elevation from $180^{\circ}$.
